clue.text: Old European money I check for friar

parts.note: the franc was the currency of France and Belgium before the euro
to scan is to check or examine

explanation.surface: Someone checks a pile of obsolete European currency on behalf of a monk.
explanation.walkthrough: The franc was replaced by the euro, hence 'Old'. The Franciscans are the order founded by St Francis of Assisi.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the religious order founded by St Francis is a mendicant brother of that order.

clue.text: Places to meet in classes around university

indicators.note: the word for classes is placed around the letter for university, enclosing it

parts.note: in British schools a form is a class or year group

explanation.surface: Students look for places to gather between lessons on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: A FORM is a school class in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum was the public square of a Roman town, and now any venue for discussion.

clue.text: Accepted an offer by editor

parts.note: a bid is an offer of a price

explanation.surface: Someone took up a proposal made by a newspaper editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide by something is to accept or tolerate it, so the past tense matches the past participle.

clue.text: Stroll like our monarchy

explanation.surface: A walk is compared to the British system of kings and queens.
explanation.walkthrough: A constitutional is an old-fashioned word for a walk taken for health; Britain's monarchy is limited by a constitution.
explanation.definitionFit: A healthy daily walk is a constitutional, and a monarchy bound by law and parliament is constitutional.

clue.text: Daily tranquillizer and late drink

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper, and a daily is a newspaper
a downer is slang for a sedative or tranquillizing drug

explanation.surface: Someone takes a daily pill to calm down and then has a nightcap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like it describes the tranquillizer but it is a noun: a daily paper, THE SUN, a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcoholic drink taken at sunset, in the evening, is traditionally called this.

clue.text: Religious leader giving a couple of bishops religious work

indicators.note: a couple means two, so the letter for bishop appears twice

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
OT is the Old Testament, a religious work

explanation.surface: A church leader hands a couple of bishops a holy book.
explanation.walkthrough: OT stands for the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a monastery is its religious superior.

clue.text: No red card for arsenal, say

explanation.surface: A football referee decides not to send off a player from Arsenal.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club. Clubs are a black playing-card suit, so not a red card; the lower-case 'arsenal' disguises a proper name.
explanation.definitionFit: In a pack of playing cards the clubs suit is black, and Arsenal is an example of a football team.

clue.text: Personal strength shown in protracted legal case

parts.note: something protracted is drawn out or long
a suit is a lawsuit, a case brought in court

explanation.surface: A person's resilience is shown during a lengthy court battle.
explanation.walkthrough: In card games a long suit is one in which you hold many cards, hence a strong point.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's forte, their particular talent, is figuratively called this, from bridge hands.

clue.text: Noble bunch making pub on time

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking place
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A group of aristocrats arrives at the pub promptly.
explanation.definitionFit: The barons collectively, or the peerage as a body, form this group.

clue.text: Battle over game that links London banks

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second piece

parts.note: Waterloo was the 1815 battle where Napoleon was defeated
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: After a battle, the soldiers play a card game that connects banks of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' suggests money but means the two sides of the River Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: This crossing spans the Thames in central London, joining its north and south shores.

clue.text: It sounds like something falling, as a rule

indicators.note: the clue says the answer is pronounced the same as the word for something falling

parts.note: rain is precipitation falling from the sky

explanation.surface: A remark notes that a word is said like the name of falling weather, generally speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a rule' looks like the phrase meaning usually, but 'rule' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's period of sovereignty is their rule over the kingdom.

clue.text: Head in rare confusion — this shouldn't cause it!

parts.note: nob is old slang for the head

indicators.note: confusion signals that the letters of the following words are muddled

explanation.surface: Something so easy it shouldn't leave anyone's head in a rare muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' scrambles the six letters of 'in rare'. The definition is semi-cryptic: 'it' points back to the confusion in the head, which something easy would never cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Something requiring no thought at all is an obvious decision that won't puzzle anyone.

clue.text: Top exponent of music or some art, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters might be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A leading musician, or maybe some artistic person, is praised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges SOME ART.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguished conductor or musical virtuoso is honoured with this Italian title.

clue.text: Time and motivation for serious crime

parts.note: a reason is a motive or cause for acting

explanation.surface: An investigator looks into when and why a grave offence was committed.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country, such as plotting against the state, is a grave offence.

clue.text: Nothing new in holding things up or being obstructive

indicators.note: the letters for nothing and new are placed inside the word for holding things up

parts.note: stalling is delaying or holding things up
O, the figure zero, means nothing
taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: Nobody new is causing delays, or perhaps just blocking progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately blocking or delaying, as in refusing to answer questions, is obstructive behaviour.

clue.text: What crowd adapted for a slogan

indicators.note: adapted means changed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rally organiser wonders what the crowd turned into a chant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges WHAT CROWD.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto or rallying cry expressing a group's principle is a password-like phrase.

clue.text: Spearman butchered? Hard cheese!

indicators.note: butchered means cut up and mangled, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A man with a spear has been slaughtered, and the response is a callous 'too bad'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese!' is British slang for 'bad luck', but here it is literal: a hard Italian cheese. 'butchered' rearranges SPEARMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian grana cheese from Parma is hard and aged, often grated over pasta.

clue.text: Exotic bird — ruddy duck!

parts.note: ruddy and flaming are both mild British swear words, and both mean red
in cricket a duck is a score of zero, so it gives O

explanation.surface: Someone spots a strange bird and exclaims about a blasted duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruddy duck' is a real bird, but here 'ruddy' is a mild British oath and 'duck' is a cricket score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall pink wading bird of tropical lagoons is a striking foreign species.

clue.text: Speaking several same sounds, say?

parts.note: the clue describes a figure of speech and itself demonstrates it with its repeated S sounds

explanation.surface: A question about uttering a string of similar sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-illustrating: Speaking, several, same, sounds and say all begin with S.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating the same initial consonant in neighbouring words is this poetic device.

clue.text: Presented as showing talent

explanation.surface: Someone is described as displaying real ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given as a present has been handed over, and a person of exceptional ability is talented.

clue.text: Kind of racehorse for which going isn't suited?

definitions.text: Kind of racehorse for which going isn't suited?

parts.words: Kind of racehorse for which going isn't suited
parts.note: going is the state of the turf in racing, but read literally a horse that remains is unsuited to leaving

explanation.surface: A question about which type of horse dislikes certain ground conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing 'the going' is the condition of the track; the joke reads 'going' as departing, the opposite of remaining.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse with stamina for long races is so called, and by its name it remains rather than departs.

clue.text: Gigantic insect that flies round a couple of maidens

indicators.note: the pair of maiden letters goes round the letter A, enclosing it
a couple means two, so the maiden letter is doubled

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, abbreviated M
a moth is a winged insect

explanation.surface: A huge flying bug circles a pair of young women.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over.
explanation.definitionFit: The extinct woolly elephant gave its name to anything enormous or huge.

clue.text: One in Panama, say, and one in Caribbean country

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed inside the word for a Panama

parts.note: a Panama is a straw hat, an example of headwear
the Roman numeral I stands for one
again the Roman numeral I for one

explanation.surface: Someone is located in Panama and another in a West Indian nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Panama' looks like the country, but it is the straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: This nation shares the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic in the West Indies.

clue.text: Musician who performs like an angel?

definitions.text: Musician who performs like an angel?

parts.words: Musician who performs like an angel
parts.note: angels are traditionally pictured playing a particular stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A question about a performer whose playing is heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like an angel' sounds like praise for the quality of playing, but it means playing the same instrument angels are shown with.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays the large plucked stringed instrument associated with angels is a musician.

clue.text: Tiny republic, a resort for Romanians

indicators.note: read as re-sort, meaning sort again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small state is described as a holiday destination popular with people from Romania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday spot, but is read as re-sort, rearranging ROMANIANS.
explanation.definitionFit: This microstate enclaved in Italy is one of the world's smallest and oldest republics.

clue.text: Daft name for a woman

explanation.surface: A silly girl's name is mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone slightly mad or eccentric is crazy, and Dotty is a female first name, short for Dorothy.

clue.text: Secluded place producing negative and positive responses

parts.note: no is a negative reply
OK is a positive or affirmative reply

explanation.surface: A hidden corner is where both refusals and agreements are given.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheltered corner or recess is a hidden spot.

clue.text: One can intuitively understand fear in pitman

indicators.note: the word for fear is placed inside the word for a pitman

parts.note: a pitman works in a coal pit, a miner
dread is great fear

explanation.surface: Someone senses the anxiety of a coal miner.
explanation.definitionFit: A telepath, someone who seems to perceive others' thoughts, is said to have this gift.
